label: A build that satisfies every documented probe still leaves the continuity writer missing: validate.sh reads runtime/dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js and the doctor probes runtime/dist, while /speckit:save needs runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js. The repair both name (cd .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime && npm run build) builds the parent project only, and runtime/cli/tsconfig.json references .. as a child, so the parent never builds it. In clone B that command exited 0, runtime/dist existed, validate.sh ran to exit 1 (validated, not exit 3), and runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js did not exist.
verify: git clone --depth 1 file://$PWD /tmp/x && cd /tmp/x && npm --prefix .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit install && npm --prefix .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime run build && ls .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js

label: The most-used command has the worst failure message: in an unbuilt clone validate.sh exits 3 with 'no validation orchestrator is available' plus 'Run: cd .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime && npm run build', while generate-context.js and match-decision-table.js each exit 1 with a raw node MODULE_NOT_FOUND and a loader stack that names no build. The continuity writer is invoked as a bare node <path> in every command asset, so it has no wrapper that can diagnose.
verify: git clone --depth 1 file://$PWD /tmp/y && cd /tmp/y && node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js --help; echo $?

label: Three build entry points carry three different freshness guarantees: skill root runs a bare tsc --build, runtime/ runs prepare-build plus tsc plus finalize-dist.mjs, runtime/cli/ runs prepare-build plus tsc plus record-build. The doctor's step 0 is the skill root, the only one with no freshness step, and a bare skill-root build still made dist-freshness check report 'dist is fresh' with exit 0, so freshness in that path is mtime-derived rather than the recorded attestation record-build exists to write.
verify: npm --prefix .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit install && npm --prefix .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit run build && node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/lib/dist-freshness.cjs check --package system-spec-kit/runtime --entry validation-orchestrator; echo exit=$?

label: validate.sh's source-only fallback is unreachable for any git clone: its comment says the loader keeps source-only checkouts working, but TSX_LOADER resolves to system-spec-kit/runtime/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs and node_modules is gitignored, so a clone has neither dist nor loader. Removing it breaks nothing for a clone; its only survivors are install-without-build developer trees, where it silently runs unattested TypeScript.

doctor setup never looks at the Spec Kit build (zero matches for runtime/dist or system-spec-kit in setup.md; its only build-adjacent reporting is the advisor's staleness ladder), while the single detector is a prose line inside doctor-install-presentation.txt that no hook, CI job or session start can call. The detection story is one command, one path, one of two dists.

Command routers hide the dist dependency their own assets carry: save.md has 5 occurrences of runtime/cli/dist and handoff.md 1, while resume.md, plan.md, implement.md, complete.md and search.md have zero, yet speckit-implement.yaml and speckit-complete.yaml both invoke node .../runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js as the writer. An AI following the documented implement route meets an unannounced build dependency at the last step.
verify: for f in .skilled/commands/speckit/*.md; do echo "$(grep -c 'runtime/cli/dist' $f) $f"; done | sort -rn

label: dist/ is gitignored and untracked (0 files under git ls-files), while runtime/cli/runtime is a tracked symlink (mode 120000, blob 85d8c32f) to ../dist, so every clone ships a dangling link and no target

The doctor step 0 command block is correct as written: install then skill-root build both exit 0 and produce runtime/dist and runtime/cli/dist, because the skill-root build is a tsc --build over project references. An earlier apparent failure was caused by an install --dry-run in the probe, not by the repository
